relevance_reason: Reports PLOD2 mutations in Bruck syndrome families and in AR-OI patients, which directly characterises BRKS2.

findings.statement: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) screened 6 consanguineous Bruck syndrome families and found changes in PLOD2 or FKBP10 in every case. Two probands carried a homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2. The authors concluded that specifically inactivating the longer PLOD2 protein isoform is enough to cause Bruck syndrome.
quotes: we sought mutations in six consanguineous BS families and detected changes in either PLOD2 or FKBP10 in all cases

Two probands were found with a homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a of PLOD2, indicating that specific inactivation of the longer protein isoform encoded by this gene is sufficient to cause BS

variants.as_reported: homozygous frameshift mutation in the alternative exon 13a

findings.statement: In a patient with autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta, Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) used homozygosity mapping followed by candidate gene analysis to identify a homozygous donor splice site mutation in PLOD2.
quotes: by homozygosity mapping, followed by a candidate gene approach, we identified a homozygous donor splice site mutation in PLOD2 in a patient with autosomal-recessive OI (AR-OI)

findings.statement: Puig-Hervás et al. (2012) found compound heterozygous PLOD2 mutations in 2 brothers. One brother had mild autosomal recessive OI and the other had mild Bruck syndrome. The authors concluded that, besides causing Bruck syndrome, PLOD2 is associated with AR-OI phenotypes of variable severity.
quotes: Screening of additional samples also revealed compound heterozygous mutations in PLOD2 in two brothers, one affected with mild AR-OI and the other with mild BS
Thus, PLOD2 in addition to causing BS is also associated with AR-OI phenotypes of variable severity.

relevance_reason: Reports a patient with Bruck syndrome type 2 who carries a novel homozygous PLOD2 mutation, and describes his clinical and biochemical findings.

findings.statement: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) reported a boy with Bruck syndrome. At birth he had congenital contractures with pterygia, along with severe osteopenia resembling osteogenesis imperfecta and multiple fractures. The authors suggested that the combination of pterygia and bone fragility implies a role for telopeptide lysyl hydroxylation in prenatal joint formation and morphogenesis.
quotes: We report on a boy who had congenital contractures with pterygia at birth and severe OI-like osteopenia and multiple fractures.
it suggests that telopeptide lysyl hydroxylation must be involved in prenatal joint formation and morphogenesis

findings.statement: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) found that the urine of their patient with Bruck syndrome contained high amounts of hydroxyproline but low amounts of collagen crosslink degradation products. They proposed that measuring collagen degradation products in urine, together with PLOD2 mutation analysis, may be used to diagnose Bruck syndrome and to distinguish it from osteogenesis imperfecta.
quotes: His urine contained high amounts of hydroxyproline but low amounts of collagen crosslinks degradation products
Collagen degradation products in urine and mutation analysis of PLOD2 may be used to diagnose BS and differentiate it from OI.

findings.statement: In a boy with Bruck syndrome, Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) identified a novel homozygous mutation in the PLOD2 gene that results in an arg598-to-his (R598H) substitution. The mutation lies next to 2 previously reported mutations, Gly601Val and Thr608Ile, and the authors suggested that this region is a functionally important hotspot in PLOD2.
quotes: he was shown to be homozygous for a novel mutation leading to an Arg598His substitution in PLOD2
The mutation is adjacent to the two mutations previously reported (Gly601Val and Thr608Ile), suggesting a functionally important hotspot in PLOD2.

findings.statement: Ha-Vinh et al. (2004) noted that Bruck syndrome is genetically heterogeneous. One locus had been mapped to 17p12 (BS type 1), while mutations in PLOD2 on 3q23-q24 cause BS type 2. They noted that it was still uncertain what proportion of cases falls into each type, and that phenotypic correlations were lacking.
quotes: One BS locus has been mapped at 17p12, but more recently, two mutations in the lysyl hydroxylase 2 gene (PLOD2, 3q23-q24) have been identified in BS, showing genetic heterogeneity.
The proportion of BS cases linked to 17p22 (BS type 1) or caused by mutations in PLOD2 (BS type 2) is still uncertain, and phenotypic correlations are lacking.

relevance_reason: Identifies PLOD2 mutations as the cause of Bruck syndrome (pyridinoline deficiency in bone collagen), defining the molecular basis of BRKS2.

findings.statement: By analyzing the genetic defect of Bruck syndrome, which is characterized by a pyridinoline deficiency in bone collagen, van der Slot et al. (2003) identified 2 missense mutations in exon 17 of the PLOD2 gene, thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase (TLH) gene.
quotes: By analyzing the genetic defect of Bruck syndrome, which is characterized by a pyridinoline deficiency in bone collagen, we found two missense mutations in exon 17 of PLOD2, thereby identifying PLOD2 as a putative TLH gene.

findings.statement: van der Slot et al. (2003) noted that Bruck syndrome is characterized by a deficiency of pyridinoline cross-links in bone collagen, which are derived from hydroxylated lysine residues within the collagen telopeptides.
quotes: Bruck syndrome, which is characterized by a pyridinoline deficiency in bone collagen
The deposited collagen shows an increase in pyridinoline cross-links, which are derived from hydroxylated lysine residues within the telopeptides.

findings.statement: van der Slot et al. (2003) found that PLOD2 mRNA was highly increased in fibroblasts derived from fibrotic skin of systemic sclerosis patients and that the matrix deposited by these fibroblasts had increased pyridinoline cross-link levels, demonstrating a link between PLOD2 mRNA levels and hydroxylation of telopeptide lysine residues.
quotes: we investigated fibroblasts derived from fibrotic skin of systemic sclerosis (SSc) patients and found that PLOD2 mRNA is highly increased indeed

increased pyridinoline cross-link levels were found in the matrix deposited by SSc fibroblasts, demonstrating a clear link between mRNA levels of the putative TLH gene (PLOD2) and the hydroxylation of lysine residues within the telopeptides

relevance_reason: Reports the biochemical defect (underhydroxylation of telopeptide lysines in bone collagen) and maps a Bruck syndrome locus to chromosome 17p12, which defines Bruck syndrome 2.

findings.statement: Bank et al. (1999) described Bruck syndrome as characterized by osteoporosis, joint contractures, fragile bones, and short stature.
quotes: Bruck syndrome is characterized by the presence of osteoporosis, joint contractures, fragile bones, and short stature.

findings.statement: In Bruck syndrome patients, Bank et al. (1999) found that lysine residues within the telopeptides of type I collagen in bone were underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking, whereas lysine residues in the triple helix were normally modified. In contrast, cartilage and ligament showed unaltered telopeptide hydroxylation, as evidenced by normal crosslinking patterns.
quotes: We report that lysine residues within the telopeptides of collagen type I in bone are underhydroxylated, leading to aberrant crosslinking, but that the lysine residues in the triple helix are normally modified.
In contrast to bone, cartilage and ligament show unaltered telopeptide hydroxylation as evidenced by normal patterns of crosslinking.

phenotypes.text: underhydroxylation of bone collagen telopeptide lysines

findings.statement: Bank et al. (1999) concluded that collagen crosslinking is regulated primarily by tissue-specific enzymes that hydroxylate only telopeptide lysine residues, and suggested that Bruck syndrome results from deficiency of a bone-specific telopeptide lysyl hydroxylase.
quotes: The results provide compelling evidence that collagen crosslinking is regulated primarily by tissue-specific enzymes that hydroxylate only telopeptide lysine residues and not those destined for the helical portion of the molecule.

findings.statement: By a genome screen in a family with affected sibs, Bank et al. (1999) identified a single region on chromosome 17p12 where all affected sibs shared a cluster of haplotypes identical by descent, and proposed this as the Bruck syndrome locus and the location of the bone telopeptidyl lysyl hydroxylase gene.
quotes: A genome screen identified only a single region on chromosome 17p12 where all affected sibs shared a cluster of haplotypes identical by descent; this might be the BS (Bruck syndrome) locus and consequently the region where bone telopeptidyl lysyl hydroxylase is located.
